sentences.text: Madan Mohan Kundu vs Unknown on 25 September, 2014

Author: Subhro Kamal Mukherjee Bench: Subhro Kamal Mukherjee S/L. 155.
tember 25, 2014. C.R.M. 12493 of 2014 ss.

In re: An application for bail under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure filed on September 05, 2014 in connection with Nabadwip Police Station Case No. 343 of 2014 dated June 06, 2014 under Sections 269/270/272/120B/34 of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 59/63 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
And In the matter of: Madan Mohan Kundu ...Petitioner.
Mr. Jay Prakash Mondal, Mr. Prasenjit Debnath ...for the petitioner.
Heard the learned advocates appearing on behalf of the respective parties.

The petitioner is seeking bail in connection with a case relating to offences punishable under Sections 269/270/272/120B/34 of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 59/63 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006.
It is submitted by the learned advocate for the petitioners that the accused/petitioner is in custody for 111 days and the investigation is complete.
Therefore, further detention of the petitioner is not necessary.

Having considered the case diary and the materials on record and, particularly, when the petitioner is in custody for 111 days and the investigation is complete, we are of the opinion that further detention of the accused/petitioner is not necessary and he may be granted bail.

Therefore, the accused/petitioner, namely, Madan Mohan Kundu, be released on bail upon furnishing bond of ` 10,000/- (Rupees ten thousand) only with two sureties of like amount, one of whom must be local, to the satisfaction of the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate at Krishnagar,
District: Nadia, on condition that the petitioner shall attend the court on each and every occasion unless prevented by sufficient cause.
The application for bail is, thus, allowed.
